programme: HEY1 and HES4 are both canonical Notch-pathway bHLH effector genes (the HES/HEY family induced by the Notch intracellular domain). HEY1's own 28-gene target set includes NOTCH1, NOTCH2, NOTCH4 and HES1 — the network is capturing Notch pathway autoregulation and downstream engagement (BMP2, ACVR1, MDM2), not just a co-expressed pair.
role_in_a: No Open Targets association and no retrieved paper places HEY1 or HES4 in fibromyalgia. The only basis for a role here is Notch's general function in blood: HES/HEY-driven signalling governs lymphocyte lineage decisions and T-cell activation states in circulating immune cells, which is where the fibromyalgia network was built — but this is inferred from Notch biology in general, not documented for this disease.
role_in_b: Well documented. HEY1 sits at the 95th percentile of Open Targets association scores for glioblastoma, and the Notch2-Hey1 axis is directly reported to drive radioresistance in glioblastoma (PMID 39501373); Notch/HES-HEY signalling more broadly is reviewed as a regulator of glioma stem-cell biology and progression via non-coding RNA control (PMID 38279763).
shared_axis: If real, the shared axis would have to run through Notch signalling operating separately in two different cellular contexts — glioma stem cells/tumour microenvironment in glioblastoma, and circulating lymphocytes in blood-sampled fibromyalgia — since nothing in the record ties a fibromyalgia phenotype to Notch activity specifically.
reasoning: The two-factor module is a real, nameable pathway and HEY1 is independently and specifically placed in glioblastoma by two papers on Notch-driven radioresistance and ncRNA regulation. But HES4 has no direct placement anywhere, no factor in this list has any Open Targets or literature record in fibromyalgia, and the diseases share no documented anatomical or clinical reason to co-opt this pathway — the fibromyalgia side of the story rests on general Notch/lymphocyte biology rather than anything retrieved.
support: PMID 39501373 — reports a Notch2-Hey1 axis driving radioresistance in glioblastoma, placing HEY1 mechanistically in the disease; PMID 38279763 — reviews non-coding RNA regulation of the Notch pathway, including HEY1, in glioblastoma. No paper places HES4, or any factor, in fibromyalgia.
how_to_falsify: Treat glioblastoma cells and fibromyalgia-patient PBMCs in parallel with a gamma-secretase inhibitor (or direct HEY1/HES4 knockdown) and measure the shared Notch target genes (NOTCH1/2/4, HES1, BMP2, MDM2). A genuine shared programme predicts coordinated, dose-dependent loss of these targets in both cell types; a coincidental statistical overlap predicts the targets move in glioblastoma cells but show no functional Notch dependency in the fibromyalgia PBMCs.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (fibromyalgia) versus brain (glioblastoma), so even a real Notch signal would run through different cell types with no evidence here that the same cellular programme is active in both. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 32 patient-group comparisons, limiting how independently this concordance has been replicated. All twelve factors, HEY1 and HES4 included, have no Open Targets or retrieved-literature record in fibromyalgia at all, so the disease-A side of this account is inference, not evidence. The two factors with the highest recurrence, HOXD1 (22/32) and RFXANK (20/32), are excluded from this account because their target sets (MOG/KRAS/SOS1/ITGB1/MLH1/SOCS1, and the RFX/CIITA MHC-II machinery) do not cohere with the Notch story, so this account explains only part of the observed concordance. The tissue-generic exclusion list removes vascular/generic regulators (ETS1, ERG, EPAS1, FOS, MEF2C, NFATC1, among others) and the single-view exclusion list is unrelated to Notch signalling, so the account is not an artefact of either filter.
